'''Almgren isomorphism theorem''' is a result in [[geometric measure theory]] and [[algebraic topology]] about the topology of the space of [[Flat convergence|flat cycles]] in a Riemannian manifold.

The theorem plays a fundamental role in the [[Almgren–Pitts min-max theory]] as it establishes existence of topologically non-trivial families of cycles, which were used by [[Frederick J. Almgren Jr.]], [[Jon T. Pitts]] and others to prove existence of (possibly singular) [[Minimal surface|minimal submanifolds]] in every Riemannian manifold. In the special case of the space of null-homologous codimension 1 cycles with mod 2 coefficients on a closed Riemannian manifold Almgren isomorphism theorem implies that it is weakly homotopy equivalent to 
the infinite [[real projective space]].<ref>*{{Citation
 | last=White
 | first=Brian
 | title=The mathematics of F. J. Almgren, Jr.

==Statement of the theorem==
Let M be a [[Riemannian manifold]]. Almgren isomorphism theorem asserts that the m-th [[homotopy group]] of the space of [[Flat convergence|flat]] k-dimensional cycles in M is isomorphic to the (m+k)-th dimensional [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] group of M. This result is a generalization of the [[Dold–Thom theorem]], which can be thought of as the k=0 case of Almgren's ([[#{{harvid|Almgren|1962a}}|1962a (ver. PhD thesis)]],<ref>{{harv|Li|2019}}</ref>[[#{{harvid|Almgren|1962b}}|1962b (ver. Topology (Elsevier)]]<ref>{{harv|Friedlander|Lawson|2009}}</ref>)<ref>{{harv|White|1997}}</ref> theorem.
The isomorphism is defined as follows. Let G be an abelian group and <math>Z_k(M;G)</math> denote the space of flat cycles with coefficients in group G. To each family of cycles <math>f: S^m \rightarrow Z_k(M;G)</math> we associate an (m+k)-cycle C as follows. Fix a fine [[Triangulation (topology)|triangulation]] T of <math>S^m</math>. To each vertex v in the 0-skeletion of T we associate a cycle f(v). To each edge E in the 1-skeleton of T with ∂E=v-w we associate a (k+1)-chain with boundary f(v)-f(w) of minimal mass. We proceed this way by induction over the skeleton of T. The sum of all chains corresponding to m-dimensional faces of T will be the desired (m+k)-cycle C. Even though the choices of triangulation and minimal mass fillings were not unique, they all result in an (m+k)-cycle in the same homology class.<ref>Guth, L. The Width-Volume Inequality. GAFA Geom. funct. anal. 17, 1139–1179 (2007)</ref>
